3.text: the natives say that if a person falls asleep immediately after eating mushrooms,

4.text: they will work more effectively, and in a short time he will awaken more

5.text: thoroughly under their influence. The intoxication has three stages. In the

6.text: first the person feels pleasantly excited. His agility increases, and he displays

7.text: more physical strength than normally. Reindeer-hunters of the Middle Anadyr

8.text: told me that before starting in canoes in pursuit of animals, they would chew

9.text: agaric because that made them more nimble on the hunt. A native fellow-

10.text: traveller of mine, after taking agaric, would lay aside his snow-shoes and

11.text: walk through the deep snow hour after hour by the side of his dogs for the

12.text: mere pleasure of exercise, and without any feeling of fatigue. During this

13.text: period the agaric-eater sings and dances. He frequently bursts into loud

14.text: peals of laughter without any apparent reason. It is a state altogether of

15.text: noisy joviality. His face acquires a darker hue and twitches nervously; his

16.text: eyes are now contracted, and again almost bursting from their sockets; his

17.text: mouth puckers and grins or spreads into a broad smile.

18.text: Flashes of the second stage often appear early, shortly after the first

19.text: traces of intoxication become visible; indeed, all three stages are frequently

20.text: intermingled. This is noticeable especially among elderly inveterate agaric-

21.text: eaters. During the second stage the intoxicated person hears strange voices

22.text: bidding him perform more or less incongruous actions; he sees the spirits of

23.text: fly-agaric and talks to them. He still recognizes surrounding objects, however,

24.text: and when talked to is able to answer. All things appear to him increased

25.text: in size. For instance, when entering a room and stepping over the door-sill,

26.text: he will raise his feet exceedingly high. The handle of a knife seems to him

27.text: so big that he wants to grasp it with both hands.

28.text: The spirits of fly-agaric have an outward appearance similar to that of

29.text: the actual mushrooms, and the agaric-eater feels impelled to imitate them.

30.text: For example, I saw one man suddenly snatch a small narrow bag and pull

31.text: it with all his might over his head, trying to break through the bottom. He

32.text: was evidently imitating the mushroom bursting forth from the ground. Another

33.text: walked around with his neck drawn in, and assured every one that he had

34.text: no head. He would bend his knees and move very quickly, swinging his

35.text: arms violently about. This was in imitation of the spirits of fly-agaric, who

36.text: are supposed to have no necks or legs, but stout cylindrical bodies which

38.text: The spirits of fly-agaric are fond of playing practical jokes on men under

39.text: their influence. They begin with asking for homage either for themselves or

40.text: for surrounding objects, — the hills, the river, the moon, etc. Then they

41.text: show some of the objects under a delusive aspect. When asked why this

42.text: strange change has occurred, the spirits answer that it portends danger to

43.text: the man’s life unless he makes obeisance in a particular way. To illustrate.
